scope: Follow-up research on the unresolved 2016 Kindle full publication date and the 2016 Kindle -> Neurodiversity Claim 2 compatible binding after D13.

publication_date_assessment.finding: Goodreads continues to identify the 98-page Kindle edition as published on 2016-07-03. Singer's own bibliography identifies the work as a 2016 Kindle edition, and Singer's dated 2016-07-16 announcement confirms that she had republished the thesis on Kindle by that date. No stronger first-party or edition-level bibliographic source inspected in this pass independently supplies the exact day-level date.
publication_date_assessment.reason_not_ready: The schema requires a full YYYY-MM-DD date. The exact day remains supported only by secondary catalogue data, so promoting 2016-07-03 would flatten a material evidence-strength distinction already preserved by D11-D13.

claim_2_binding_assessment.finding: Singer's July 2016 announcement identifies the announced Kindle edition as the republished thesis plus a new introduction and reproduces a publisher's blurb describing the work as operating from post-modern, social-constructionist, feminist and disability-rights perspectives while criticizing social-constructionist fundamentalism. Dwyer (2022), a peer-reviewed Human Development article, cites Singer (2016) by Kindle location and characterises Singer's position as rejecting a simple Medical Model versus Social Model binary and taking a middle ground. Dwyer's later discussion separately proposes a middle-ground neurodiversity approach that can recognize disability, supports and limited interventions without making normalization or cure the goal; those later prescriptive details are Dwyer's proposal and are not attributed here to Singer.
claim_2_binding_assessment.edition_specificity: Singer's announcement is first-party evidence for the identity of the 2016 Kindle edition and hosts the publisher's framing description; the peer-reviewed route explicitly cites Singer 2016 with Kindle location numbers rather than relying on the later 2017 print edition.
limitations: Singer's announcement is first-party for the edition identity but reproduces a publisher's blurb for much of the framing description; it is not a page-level copy of the edition itself.
Dwyer 2022 is a secondary scholarly interpretation, although it cites Singer 2016 with Kindle location numbers.
Dwyer's discussion of disability, supports, interventions, normalization and cure extends beyond the specific middle-ground proposition that Dwyer directly attributes to Singer 2016.
Acceptance would remain a compatible Evidence Contribution binding, not proof that every contemporary neurodiversity position shares Singer's framing.

next_decision_candidates.question: Accept the 2016 Kindle -> Neurodiversity Claim 2 compatible binding now that first-party edition evidence and a secondary scholarly interpretation grounded in Singer 2016 Kindle locations materially strengthen the compatibility case, while keeping the 2016 full publication date unresolved?

preserved_blockers.2016_full_date: 2016-07-03 remains a secondary-catalogue candidate and is not promoted by this research pass.
preserved_blockers.uncertainty_shape: Neurodiversity and Autism list-valued uncertainty mapping remains unresolved/deferred.
preserved_blockers.structural_confidence: D6 continues to forbid inferred/defaulted structural confidence.
preserved_blockers.adhd_dependency: Neurodiversity broader_than -> adhd remains outside the D5 pair.
